newsitem.title: USA: Troy, N.Y sees more savings from refinancing-paper.
newsitem.headline: Troy, N.Y sees more savings from refinancing-paper.

text.p: Troy, N.Y., which got its bondholders to agree to waive a payment due Sept 15, expects to save more than it had anticipated from the restructuring plan, Albany Times Union reported Thursday.
The pact, which the City Council is expected to vote on Wednesday, would save the city $18 million, Mayor Mark Pattison told the paper.

Troy, which in July had about $90 million of long-term debt outstanding, at first estimated it would save $11 million by refinancing about $35 million of leaseback debt over 27 years. The September 15 payment that was waived for this leaseback debt totaled $1.4 million.
The agreement calls for the city to pay a maximum of $74 million in principal and interest, with no more than $6 million of debt service each year.

However, when city officials analyzed the terms of the agreement, they found that the $74 million level would be reached in 2021, more than one year before the orignal expiration date, the paper said.
Due to the restructuring plan, Troy, which raised taxes 27 percent in 1996, does not expect to have to do so in 1997, the mayor added.
